text:
maya: heads up — customer reported our sampleapp stream returning duplicate partial tokens and occasional JSON parse errors behind corporate proxy. repro steps included chrome on windows + vpn.
eli: hmm. any logs?
maya: pasted a trimmed server log: 
```
2026-03-20T14:02:11.123Z INFO stream: client_conn=42 chunk="data: {"id":1,"text":"Hel"}\n"
2026-03-20T14:02:11.124Z INFO stream: client_conn=42 chunk="\n"
2026-03-20T14:02:11.125Z INFO stream: client_conn=42 chunk="data: {"id":1,"text":"lo"}\n"
```
maya: looks like CRLF split produced an empty chunk between partial tokens. client reassembly in JS treats blank line as event separator and re-emits partial payloads.
sam: is this the fetch SSE client in sampleapp? or EventSource?
maya: sampleapp uses custom fetch-based SSE (we added for auth refresh parity). here's simplified client snippet: 
```js
const res = await fetch(url, {headers});
const reader = res.body.getReader();
while(true){
  const {done, value} = await reader.read();
  if(done) break;
  const str = new TextDecoder().decode(value);
  // naive: split on "\n\n" and JSON.parse each event
}
```
sam: naive split is the culprit — corp proxies sometimes inject an extra CRLF or buffer boundary that yields an empty token. We should tolerate empty events and coalesce fragments based on event id/last-event-id.
jonah: also observed with auth retry — when token refresh triggers a new connection, some clients requeue partial bytes and then merge with new bytes without resetting parser state, leading to token duplication.
eli: do we have a parity gap between browsers and node? Node fetch returns chunks differently. Our node SDK had a fix to buffer until we see a complete JSON object (matching braces) — could copy logic.
maya: customer repro: they see garbled JSON like `{"id":1,"text":"Hel` then later `lo"}{"id":2,...` which crashes the sampleapp parser.
ci-bot: test-run failed: sampleapp-integration/streaming-reassembly on windows-proxy matrix — 3 failures.
jonah: proposed quick fixes: 1) treat empty chunk as no-op, 2) implement incremental JSON framing (accumulate until braces balanced), 3) reset parser state on auth refresh or expose explicit resume token handling.
eli: +1. Also add a small e2e test with a proxy that injects extra CRLF and splits codepoints mid-UTF8 to catch decoder edgecases.
sam: i can PR a tiny parser util to both node and browser sdks. keep it small: accumulate buffer, try parse when we see `\n\n` or when braces balanced, drop empty events.
maya: can we also add logging that tags whether the connection was re-auth'd so we can triage auth-related merges?
jonah: yes — server should emit `:auth-refresh` comment line when we trigger re-auth, client should reset after that marker.
devx-bot: created issue RDW-1873: "sampleapp: SSE parser resilient to proxy CRLF and auth-retry reassembly" and assigned to sam.
maya: thanks — customer notified that we found a workaround (disable proxy compression) but we should fix upstream.
eli: ok i'll add node/browser parity test and include in CI matrix. can we get a small postmortem note after fix? keep it short for docs.
sam: on it, will open PR today. :thumbsup:
